task.description: Fresh full re-check of lib/letflow/design/iss0911-start-instance-dialog-exact-lookup.md after rework 1 (which folds two independently-writing effects into a single one, guarded by a lookupWroteDefinitionId ref, to close the race REVIEWER found in the original design -- read handoffs/WF03-ISS0911-20260930/step-02-code-designer-rework1.json and the referenced step-03d-reviewer.json for the full original FAIL). Do not just check that the specific race REVIEWER found is closed -- independently trace the new merged effect's full priority order (found / not_found-error / idle-loading-with-ref-check) yourself against every possible transition sequence (e.g. what happens on a rapid found -> not_found -> found sequence from fast retyping; what happens if the ref is stale from a PREVIOUS dialog-open session) to confirm no new race was introduced by the fix. Re-run the full Step 2 design gate over the whole document.
acceptance_criteria: the fix calls definitionsApi.getActive(name) (or an equivalent exact-match backend lookup) keyed on the dialog's own typed value, not the page-level filtered list
a race-guard against out-of-order async responses (rapid typing) is explicitly designed, not left implicit
the version field's loading/not-found/found states are all specified

a single write path for startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId is designed, with no possibility of the new effect's own setSearchParams call re-triggering a second, independent effect that transiently desyncs the two values

gate_history.summary: Two independent effects both wrote startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId; the new effect's setSearchParams call re-triggered the old effect before its cache had the new id, transiently blanking the version display -- caught by REVIEWER (Step 3d), not by this design gate itself.
issues: The design's own §1 asserted the old effect was 'already-correct, untouched' without accounting for the new effect's setSearchParams side effect reactivating it
gate_history.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER for design rework: fold both effects into a single write path.
